answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs or vote on disputes. The protocol caps each stake’s influence and slashes it when a bonded challenge proves fraud, so creating a thousand names does not multiply voting power: the attacker must acquire and immobilize more capital, then risks losing it. A relic-market analogy helps: ivory tokens may decorate a ledger’s kernel, but only the locked stake earns weight. This raises the cost of Sybils without assuming names are unique.
